chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever divorces contrary to the Sunnah shall be returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, even if his nose is rubbed in the dust.

key_terms.السُّنَّة: The Sunnah — the established prophetic practice and rulings regarding divorce procedure
key_terms.رَغِمَ أَنْفُهُ: His nose is rubbed in the dust — classical Arabic idiom meaning 'even against his will'
key_terms.رُدَّ: To be returned/rejected — a legal term indicating the nullification of the divorce
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of Allah (the Quran) — the primary legal source to which invalid divorces are returned

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about a divorce that does not follow the Sunnah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues an authoritative ruling that any divorce performed contrary to the established Sunnah is legally void and must be reversed, referring the matter back to the Quran. The phrase 'even if his nose is rubbed in the dust' is a classical Arabic idiom for 'even against one's will,' emphasizing the mandatory nature of this ruling. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that divorce must conform strictly to the conditions laid down in the Quran and the prophetic Sunnah, or it is deemed invalid.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Al Magra, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who divorces to other than the Sunnah, should be returned to the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, even if his nose it to be forced’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from abu al=Mighra’ from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who does not divorce according to Sunnah must be returned to the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, even though he may refuse.’”
